summary: This study aims to characterize healthy human retinal aging in vivo using advanced adaptive optics ophthalmoscopy (AOO) imaging, clinical imaging, and visual function testing, focusing on retinal pigment epithelium (RPE)-photoreceptor cellular organization and microscopic autofluorescence variation with age and wavelength. The study will produce the largest quantitative in vivo normative dataset of AOO cell-based metrics to date, enabling the development of new analysis tools for evaluating emerging therapies for age-related macular degeneration (AMD). The study will also compare normal photoreceptor topography and RPE cell morphometry to clinically defined early AMD to identify the earliest cellular changes that differentiate normal aging from early AMD.
